chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A meal which my Muslim brother eats with me is more beloved to me than if I were to free a neck.

key_terms.أُعْتِقَ: To be freed (as in freeing a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual merit of sharing a meal with a Muslim brother according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the simple act of sharing a meal with a fellow believer above the major act of manumitting a slave, underscoring the profound spiritual weight of maintaining kinship (silat al-rahibm) through daily hospitality. This comparison reflects the Shia emphasis on the tangible, social dimensions of faith, where strengthening communal bonds is viewed as a direct path to divine pleasure. The narration serves as a practical reminder that consistent, modest acts of generosity towards one's 'brother in faith' carry immense merit in the sight of the Ahl al-Bayt.
